after:
name: first_graphics
description: Capture the two-box first-graphics template using its shipped code and
  shaders.
operations:
- create:
    box: first_graphics_renderer
    name: 1 · Launch the renderer
    frame:
      x: 70.0
      y: 70.0
      w: 350.0
      h: 100.0
    properties:
      code: |-
        // Launch this box first: Alt+Up (Option+Up on macOS).
        prop<Window>(window)
        prop<Renderer>(renderer)
        once.renderer {
            window = Window("Field · first native graphics")
            Renderer(window)
        }
        start(renderer::run)
- create:
    box: first_graphics_triangle
    name: 2 · Launch the triangle
    frame:
      x: 70.0
      y: 270.0
      w: 350.0
      h: 100.0
    properties:
      code: |-
        // A module connects this box's vertex and fragment shaders to its meshes.
        // Re-launching replaces the module under this box's name.
        renderer += moduleHere {
            primitiveType = triangle_strip
            +Mesh("triangle") {
                // Three clip-space positions (-1..1), three RGBA colours and one triangle.
                set(3, 3) {
                    pos.add(0, 0, 0, 0.5, 0, 0, 0.5, 0.5, 0)
                    3 {
                        col.add(0, it / 3.0, 1 - it / 3.0, 1)
                    }
                    tri.add(0, 1, 2)
                }
            }
        }

        /*
         Switch to the shaders with F1 or Ctrl+P:
         [[property vertex]]
         [[property fragment]]
         */
      vertex: "#version 450\nlayout (location = 0) in vec3 pos;\n\nlayout (location = 1) in vec4 col;\nlayout (location = 0) out vec4 fcol;\n\n// pos is already in clip space; col is passed to the fragment shader.\n\nvoid main()\n{\n\n    fcol = col;\n    gl_Position = vec4(pos, 1);\n}\n"
      fragment: "#version 450\nlayout(location = 0) out vec4 uFragColor;\n\nlayout(location = 0) in vec4 fcol;\nvoid main()\n{\n    uFragColor = vec4(1.0, 0.8, 0.4, 1.0)* fcol;\n}"
- connect:
    parent: first_graphics_renderer
    child: first_graphics_triangle

before:
name: first_graphics_native
description: Launch the shipped first-graphics renderer and triangle for its native
  screenshot.
operations:
- create:
    box: first_graphics_renderer
    name: 1 · Launch the renderer
    frame:
      x: 70.0
      y: 70.0
      w: 350.0
      h: 100.0
    properties:
      code: "// Launch this box first: Alt+Up (Option+Up on macOS).\nprop<Window>(window)\n\
        prop<Renderer>(renderer)\nonce.renderer {\n    window = Window(\"Field · first\
        \ native graphics\")\n    Renderer(window)\n}\nstart(renderer::run)\n"
- create:
    box: first_graphics_triangle
    name: 2 · Launch the triangle
    frame:
      x: 70.0
      y: 270.0
      w: 350.0
      h: 100.0
    properties:
      code: "// this is almost as simple as drawing a triangle gets here. First a\
        \ shader:\nvar module = moduleHere {\n    primitiveType = triangle_strip\n\
        }\n\n    // then a mesh\nvar m  = Mesh()\n\n    // then some connection\n\
        module += m named \"my mesh\"\nrenderer += module\n\n/*\nThis gets us everything\
        \ we need to start rendering things. In particular, we get a vertex shader:\n\
        \n[[property vertex]]\n*/\n\n    // and a fragment shader:\n\n/*\n[[property\
        \ fragment]]\n*/\n\n// you can edit these by switching to these properties\
        \ in the editor `f1` or `ctrl-P`.\n\n// and then 3 vertices and one triangle\
        \ strip consisting of 3 indices\nm.set(3, 3) {\n    pos.add(0,0,0, 0.5,0,0,\
        \ 0.5,0.5,0)\n\n    // for a flourish, we have some color as well\n    3 {\n\
        \        col.add(0,it/3.0,1-it/3.0,1)\n    }\n    tri.add(0,1,2)\n}\n"
      vertex: |
        #version 450
        layout (location = 0) in vec3 pos;

        layout (location = 1) in vec4 col;
        layout (location = 0) out vec4 fcol;

        void main()
        {
            fcol = col;
            // pos is already in clip space; this triangle needs no camera transform.
            gl_Position = vec4(pos, 1);
        }
      fragment: "#version 450\nlayout(location = 0) out vec4 uFragColor;\n\nlayout(location\
        \ = 0) in vec4 fcol;\nvoid main()\n{\n    uFragColor = vec4(1.0, 0.8, 0.4,\
        \ 1.0)* fcol;\n}"
- connect:
    parent: first_graphics_renderer
    child: first_graphics_triangle
- launch:
    box: first_graphics_renderer
    property: code
    type: code
- wait:
    frames: 3
- launch:
    box: first_graphics_triangle
    property: code
    type: code
- wait:
    frames: 4

before:
name: first_steps
description: Capture the first-steps template, using its shipped code.
operations:
- create:
    box: first_steps_drawing
    name: First steps · a moving drawing
    frame:
      x: 70.0
      y: 70.0
      w: 350.0
      h: 100.0
    properties:
      code: |
        // Launch: Alt+Up. Stop: Alt+Down. On a Mac, Alt is Option.
        var petals = 5
        petals = 5 // Change this 5 to 8, then press Alt+Enter on this line while the drawing runs.
        println(petals) // Field shows this value beside the code.
        var phase = 0.0

        loop {
            phase += 0.045
            // Each curve is a little further into the wave: together they make a ribbon.
            val ribbon =
                (0..23).map { layer ->
                    val depth = layer / 23.0
                    fline {
                        breakNext()
                        for (i in 0..180) {
                            val angle = i * Math.PI / 90.0
                            val wave = Math.sin(petals * angle + phase - 4.0 * depth)
                            val radius = 35.0 + 90.0 * depth + 18.0 * wave
                            val twist = angle + 0.4 * Math.sin(phase + 2.0 * depth)
                            val x = 160.0 + radius * Math.cos(twist)
                            val y = 160.0 + radius * Math.sin(twist)
                            lineTo(x, y)
                        }
                        thickness = 0.8
                        color = vec(0.55 + 0.4 * depth, 0.85 + 0.15 * depth, 1.0, 0.8)
                    }
                }
            lines(ribbon, w = 320.0, h = 320.0)
        }

        // Field autosaves edits. Stop, close this tab, then reopen your copy
        // from Welcome: your edited code is there; launch it to animate again.
